question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $28u+16v=\text{gcd}(28,16).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}28 & = & 16\cdot 1 & + & 12 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 16 & = & 12\cdot 1 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 12 & = & 4\cdot 3 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(16,28)=4.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =28-16 \\ 4 & =16-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =16-12 \\  & =16-(28-16) \\  & =16\cdot 2-28 \\  & =28\cdot (-1)+16\cdot 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-1$ and $v=2.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-1)+2=1.
$$
